main_text.p: Democritum autem adeo in omnigenere philosophia profecisse memorant, ut pentathlos, sive quinquertio dici posset, quod naturalia, moralia, mathematica, liberales disciplinas, artiumque omnium peritiam callebat. Hunc vero quem Plinius virum sagacem, & vita utilissimum fuisse refert dementem reputant, petulantiores in ipsum quam Aristoteles, qui ut suo tempore monstrabimus, quo maxime loco Democritus horum arbitrio delirat, ejus opinionem praefert Platonis sententia, parumne est Democritum ab Aristotele Platoni esse praelatum, & quidem in quo cachinnos Peripateticis movet? Quin eodem capite secundo libri primi de generatione Aristotelis communi veterum, & Democriti sententia ex parte suffragatus, de eo non praetermittendum dedit testimonium; cum Priscorum in scientia naturali peritiam extenuans, ita suam concludit sententiam. Ad summum de nulla mutatione, nisi superficie tenus quicquam ullus definivit, praeterquam Democritus, cui omnia curae videntur fuisse, in modo tamen, atque ratione discrepavit. Hoc Aristotelis testimonio qua parte sibi favet, memoria Democriti fruatur, qua vero officit, suspectum sit Aristotelis judicium; sicut ejusdem testimonium, cum ait veteres omnes alios de nulla mutatione quicquam nisi superficie tenus definivisse. page.notes: The text is one paragraph; the page has no first-line indent I could confirm, so no cont flag is set. The long s is rendered as a plain s throughout, as the rules require. The printed "s" and "f" look alike in places, e.g. "suam", "sententiam", "suffragatus", "testimonium", "suspectum", which were read as s. The line "omnia" reads "omni a" with a break, taken as "omnia". Two dots after "Ad" and "praetermittendum" look like ornaments or ink specks, not letters. The catchword "versis" is partly cut at the edge; read as "versis". The word "Democritus" in the phrase "praeterquam Democritus" is clear. The page number is absent, only the signature "** 4" is printed.
